dialogue.user: Hi there! I'm looking for a new book to read. I'm on a bit of a budget, so I'm hoping to spend between $0 and $15. I also want something that's generally well-liked, so a rating of at least 2 out of 5.0 would be great. What do you have that might fit the bill?

I found 10 books that fit your criteria! Here are a few that caught my eye:

*   **Happy Holiday Pounds: A Weight Loss Plan for Losing Holiday Pounds** - 5/5 stars, $14.99
*   **Ausgrenor: The first novel in the Raising Up Pharaoh series** - 5/5 stars, $14.95
*   **The Mother of My Child (Silhouette Desire, No 831)** - 5/5 stars, $6.14

Would you like to know more about any of these?

dialogue.user: Hmm, those are interesting titles! Let's start with "Ausgrenor: The first novel in the Raising Up Pharaoh series." What's that one about?
dialogue.agent:
This book is set in the Fertile Crescent at the dawn of written history and follows a group of survivors seeking refuge in the city of Ausgrenor. The story encompasses themes of survival, loyalty, and political intrigue as they face threats from invaders. It's the first in a six-novel series and aims to explore the cultural seeds of today's world. It has a 5/5 star rating and, at $14.95, is within your budget.

The reviews mention that the series is intriguing, educational, and entertaining, with themes that resonate with modern readers. One reviewer found it helpful to use the provided maps and website to keep track of the many characters and locations.

Would you like to explore other options, or perhaps learn more about this book?

result.title: Ausgrenor: The first novel in the Raising Up Pharaoh series
result.features: 5,203 years ago, cruel eastern invaders annihilate villages in the wintry Sakros Mountains. Survivors flood west into the fertile plain between the rivers, seeking refuge among its walled cities. Three shepherd boys see their families executed and flee to one of their caves, where they find eight starving girls and bodies of others. Unwilling to abandon them, the boys hide them in a remote cave in the high forest, and feed and equip them until they’re fit to travel. Weida, widowed princess of an overrun kingdom, joins them on their trek to Ausgrenor. She seeks Patros, widower-brother of her late husband. Fortified cities fall. Ausgrenor stands alone. Terrified citizens regress into savagery. Their vicious king plots to rob the rich and flee. Neighboring Bedu tribes slip away into the desert. Invaders approach. Patros is torn between ancestral loyalties and survival of his new wards. Fight or flee. Now or never. Thus begins the six-novel Raising Up Pharaoh epic, set among the emerging city-states and nations in the Fertile Crescent at the dawn of written history—as they plant the cultural seeds of today’s world. The series is written for readers of all ages. The tone is intense, yet controlled by zooming back the lens to avoid needless close-ups of violence and sexuality. The tale unfolds through the differing viewpoints of the orphans, the couple, others drawn to them, and their foes. This first book’s setting ranges across the southwestern mountains of what is now called Iran, southern Iraq between the lower Tigris and Euphrates rivers, the marshes of their delta with the Persian Gulf, and is bounded on the west by the Saudi Arabian desert. In later books, the setting expands throughout the Middle East, the Steppes, West and South Asia, and Northwest Africa. Each book has its own maps. The diverse cast speaks a pidgin of proto-Indo-European, proto-Afro-Semitic, and various lost languages such as Harappan. The pidgin is presented in modern U.S. English. The Raising Up Pharaoh novels were edited by Dr. Dennis E. Hensley PhD

top_reviews.title: An adequate evaluation necessitates that this review include all six books of the series.  Enjoy!
top_reviews.text: I read all six books of the Raising up Pharaoh series over a period of about two weeks.  The story line was so intriguing; I could hardly put them down.  I love reading; and history, wars, geography, archeology, biography, adventure, education, technology, inspiration, miracles, romance, humor and irony are all included in the events and lives of the characters of these books.  Patros, the head of the family and most admirable character, was under constant temptation and pressure to make personal and administrative decisions for himself and his people that were not in keeping with his desire to follow the will of his one god, the God of Creation.  Many other admirable characters (both Eurasian and Bedouin) were ordinary people who were subjected to the temptations and errors in judgment of all humans but were inspired and thrilled to learn what it meant to have God enter their lives and make them instrumental in his plan.  It is easy to identify with these people even today.  The most difficult aspect of reading the books for me was keeping track of the many characters and places with unfamiliar but similarly-spelled names.  Using the author’s website http://www.raisinguppharaoh.com/  in parallel was helpful in understanding their meanings.  But I found the most interesting and helpful tool was studying the maps that are included in the books to keep track of the movement and routes they traveled.  Sometimes it was difficult to keep track of the time line of the various events, because the story covered the actions and relationships of a wide variety of characters and locations.  However, the overall story was fascinating, educational and entertaining.  I recommend and consider this series a “must read” for friends and family.

dialogue.user:
That sounds pretty fascinating, especially the historical setting! I do appreciate when a book can be both educational and entertaining. And it hits my price point perfectly. It has a 5/5 rating, which is excellent.

What about "The Mother of My Child (Silhouette Desire, No 831)"? What's the genre for that one?
dialogue.agent: "The Mother of My Child (Silhouette Desire, No 831)" is a romance novel. It's priced at $6.14 and has a 5/5 star rating.

result.title: The Mother of My Child (Silhouette Desire, No 831)
result.features: BLACK SHEEP'S BABY Spence Rand may have been a member of the premier family of Marshallton, Tennessee, but he'd also been a classic teenage rebel. Not only had he dared to become passionately entangled with the housekeeper's daughter - he'd gone and fallen in love with her. Though he knew fiery, outspoken Pattie Cornell was his soul mate, Spence had left town and never looked back. Never until now, when a shocking secret revealed the truth about the venerable Rand family, and about the woman Spence hadn't been able to forget. Bracing himself to confront the past, Spence returned to Marshallton. With him was the daughter Pattie Cornell had borne - and been told she had lost...

dialogue.user:
A romance novel, eh? That's a different direction. While the price is great and the rating is perfect, I'm not sure romance is exactly what I'm in the mood for right now.

Could you tell me a bit more about "Happy Holiday Pounds: A Weight Loss Plan for Losing Holiday Pounds"? The title is a bit intriguing, but I'm curious about the content.
dialogue.agent: "Happy Holiday Pounds: A Weight Loss Plan for Losing Holiday Pounds" is a weight-loss guide focused on healthy eating and providing alternatives to sweets. It aims to help readers lose weight, particularly those "holiday pounds," year-round. It's priced at $14.99 and has a 5/5 star rating, with one reviewer mentioning they "love it" and find the sections on chocolate and wine particularly great.

result.title: Happy Holiday Pounds: A Weight Loss Plan for Losing Holiday Pounds
result.features: Have you ever wanted to lose weight, but didn't know where to start? Happy Holiday Pounds is a weight-loss book focused on helping you lose those Holiday pounds, year round! With a wealth of information on healthy eating, alternatives to dreaded "sweets," and bonus sections, this premium book can help anyone get on the right track for that "New Year's Resolution!"

top_reviews.title: Love it.
top_reviews.text: I love it. Lots of great information. I like the parts on chocolate and wine!!

dialogue.user:
While I appreciate the 5/5 rating and the fact that it's under $15, a weight loss plan isn't really what I'm looking for in a book for entertainment. I'm more in the mood for a story.

"Ausgrenor: The first novel in the Raising Up Pharaoh series" still sounds like the most promising option for me. It's within my budget, has a perfect rating, and the description sounds really engaging. I think I'll go with that one.

Ausgrenor: The first novel in the Raising Up Pharaoh series is the book I would like to purchase.<YES>
